detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Information scrambling acts as a competing process to decoherence-induced record formation; while decoherence localizes information for observers, scrambling distributes it globally, potentially masking the formation of local, redundant records.
detail.reason: Synthesizing the competitive relationship between scrambling and redundancy.
